subject: Request: BetaApps launch — throughput surge playbook & temporary quota bump
summary: External customer requests a temporary quota and routing change for a November launch; internal product/infra need to validate capacity, propose runbook, and schedule a canary window.
messages:
From: Lena Cho <lena.cho@betaapps.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-10T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Launch traffic profile + temporary quota request (Nov 15)

Alex —

Quick note from BetaApps ops: we have a hard launch scheduled for 2026-11-15 (internal marketing push + partner integrations). Based on our load tests, plan expects repetitive short bursts during onboarding flows: typical pattern is a 20-minute burst, 800–1,200 RPS (requests/sec) for that window, with an expected average of 120 RPS outside bursts. Average tokens per request ~1,200 tokens (prompt + expected generation).

Can Redwood provision a temporary rate-limit/quota increase for us for the launch day and provide a recommended canary window and rollback triggers? We're targeting a 2-hour window (09:00–11:00 PST) for canary traffic, and then open to full rollout if metrics look good.

Attached is our traffic_forecast_v2.xlsx with per-region breakdown and peak estimates. We can also sign any temporary SLA/usage agreement you need.

Thanks,
Lena Cho
Sr. Technical Program Manager — BetaApps
Ops: ops@betaapps.com

Attachments: traffic_forecast_v2.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-10T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Launch traffic profile + temporary quota request (Nov 15)

Folks — forwarding BetaApps ask. TL;DR: external forecasts bursts up to 1.2k RPS, avg 120 RPS, ~1.2k tokens/request. They want a temporary quota bump for 11/15 and a canary window 09:00–11:00 PST.

Request: can infra + product validate we can safely route this to hosted, propose an exact quota (RPS and token/min), recommended model variant(s) to use for cost / determinism, and a runbook for canary and rollback triggers. Also confirm whether we need a temporary reserved capacity allocation or we can do transient routing and throttles.

Pls reply with concrete numbers and a one-paragraph runbook (monitoring gates & rollback conditions). I'm happy to communicate the plan to BetaApps once we have internal alignment.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-10T18:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Launch traffic profile + temporary quota request (Nov 15)

Thanks for the ping. Quick take from runtime/infra: we can support the traffic pattern but need to make a few configuration changes and a short validation plan. Notes below — please review and flag if you want a different approach.

1) Recommended temporary quota: 1,500 RPS limit with a token-based ceiling of 3,000,000 tokens/min during the two-hour window. This gives ~2.5x headroom on their peak while keeping a token cap in place.

2) Routing / model variant: serve the canary traffic against a cost-stable variant (gpt-7b-q4_0) to reduce per-token latency variance. If BetaApps requires higher quality, we can offer gpt-13b-vanilla but that will reduce throughput.

3) Burst control: configure a leaky bucket with a 2-minute refill window, and a hard 2-minute cooldown if sustained error rate (5xx) > 1% or p99 latency > 1500ms.

4) Monitoring gates (must pass all):
   - p95 latency <= 500ms
   - p99 latency <= 1500ms
   - 5xx rate <= 1%
   - CPU/GPU mem util < 85% on serving pool
   - KV cache hit rate >= 60% (helps reduce cold-start token costs)

5) Rollback triggers (any):
   - p99 latency > 2s for > 2 consecutive minutes
   - 5xx rate > 3% for > 1 minute
   - GPU OOMs or node failures exceeding 1% of pool

6) Runbook steps (short):
   - Pre-launch (D-7): create temporary rate-limit policy + dedicated route, schedule capacity reservation if needed.
   - Canary (09:00 PST): enable 50% of planned quota, verify metrics for 15 minutes, then ramp to 100% over 30 minutes if gates pass.
   - Full roll (post-canary): open to full traffic with continuous anomaly detection and auto-fallback to baseline model.

I'll attach our internal "quota_request_form.pdf" (filled) to formalize the request and notify capacity planning. If product wants to change the model choice, let me know algorithmically what quality/latency tradeoff you want and I'll size the pool.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Attachments: quota_request_form.pdf (pdf)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-10T20:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Launch traffic profile + temporary quota request (Nov 15)

Thanks team — appreciated. Product notes / roadmap considerations:

- Approve the temporary quota as proposed by Dev (1,500 RPS / 3M tokens/min) for the limited window. We should serve canary traffic on the cheaper latency-stable variant (gpt-7b-q4_0) and offer an opt-in to the higher-quality variant for a subset of customers (not the default).

- We need to capture a simple rollback SLA in writing with BetaApps (15-minute rollback guarantee). Monica can own the contract note for the temporary increase.

- Operational runbook: Marcus, can you schedule the config change as a one-time scheduled job (11/15 08:45 PST) to create the temporary route and policy? Also create an alert group that notifies on-call + Alex + BetaApps ops channel for the canary window. Elastic autoscaling should be set to conservative (max additional nodes capped at 20% of pool) to avoid noisy neighbor issues.

- Post-launch: run a quick cost/regression analysis and share with BetaApps within 48 hours. We should also capture the traffic samples for quality evals (redact PII).

If everyone is aligned I suggest we lock the plan by EOD Monday and send BetaApps a formal schedule + DocuSign for the temporary quota terms.

— Lauren
Head of Product, Redwood Inference

Related runbook: https://internal.redwood.com/runbooks/launch-canary-playbook (internal)

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: lena.cho@betaapps.com, ops@betaapps.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-11T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Launch traffic profile + temporary quota request (Nov 15) — plan & next steps

Lena —

Thanks for the forecast and for the patience while we validated internally. Short version of the plan we can commit to and next steps below.

What we'll do:
- Temporary quota: 1,500 RPS with a token cap of 3,000,000 tokens/min for 2026-11-15.
- Canary window: 2026-11-15 09:00–11:00 PST. We will start at 50% of the quota for the first 15 minutes, then ramp to 100% over 30 minutes if pass gates.
- Model: default gpt-7b-q4_0 for canary (option to route 5% of traffic to gpt-13b-vanilla on request).
- Rollback triggers: p99 > 2s for 2 consecutive minutes, 5xx > 3% for 1 minute, or GPU OOMs as described in the runbook.

What we need from BetaApps (action items):
1) Sign the temporary quota terms (DocuSign): https://www.docusign.net/Sign/MockDoc/LAUNCH-5231
2) Confirm final expected peak RPS per region in the attached forecast (we reviewed the attached workbook; any last edits by 2026-11-01).
3) Share a designated on-call contact for the canary window (name + mobile).

Internal owners: Monica will own contractual language; Marcus will schedule the configuration (scheduled job at 08:45 PST on 11/15) and create alerts; Dev will own runtime changes and monitoring gates; Lauren will own post-launch QA & cost analysis; Rachel will monitor usage & billing impacts.

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the canary window and a short pre-launch checklist meeting (D-3). Thanks everyone for quick turnaround.

— Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: traffic_forecast_v2.xlsx (xlsx), quota_request_form.pdf (pdf)
